result.summary: This PR fixes CRollingBloomFilter::insert so that re-inserting an item already represented in the current generation does not advance the entry counter, which previously let a single repeated value expire unrelated entries earlier than the configured capacity implies. It also avoids double-hashing by reusing computed hashes, and adds two new unit tests covering the repeated-insert and refresh scenarios. The change is a targeted bug fix within a shared low-level utility class.
result.problem: CRollingBloomFilter is used to bound resource usage and deduplicate seen items across the node (e.g. anti-DoS tracking); the author's description explains that repeatedly inserting one value advances its generation counter without adding coverage, causing unrelated tracked entries to be evicted sooner than the filter's stated capacity, which weakens whatever protection the filter is meant to provide.

result.card: This PR fixes a correctness bug in CRollingBloomFilter::insert: repeatedly inserting the same value advanced the entry counter without adding new coverage, causing unrelated tracked items to expire earlier than the filter's stated capacity implies, per the author's description. The fix detects current-generation membership before rotating and reuses already-computed hashes to avoid double hashing, with two new unit tests demonstrating both the fixed behavior and correct refresh semantics. CRollingBloomFilter is a shared low-level primitive used for filtering/deduplication across the codebase, so a subtle capacity-eviction bug here could weaken whatever anti-DoS or dedup guarantee a consumer expects. The PR is small, self-contained, and ready for review; the only discussion so far is a reviewer (instagibbs) asking whether this addresses an observed real-world issue or is a general correctness fix, unanswered but not yet stale. No stated dependencies or blockers.
